topics.label: Opening Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture context, relevance, and historical difficulty of studying complement.

topics.label: Foundations and Core Principles of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the general architecture, naming conventions, and central biochemical hub of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the three distinct recognition pathways that generate surface-bound convertases to reach the C3 activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector Functions of Activated Complement
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the primary downstream mechanisms through which activated complement eliminates pathogens via opsonization, inflammation, and direct lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms and surface factors that protect host cells from spontaneous complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Presentations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how genetic or acquired deficiencies in various complement components lead to specific infection susceptibilities and autoimmune pathologies.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus have evolved mechanisms to disrupt, degrade, and circumvent complement defenses.

topics.label: Closing Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic marks the end of the complement lecture and previews the upcoming topic on adaptive immunity.
